 Early voting surges 45% in Tennessee during 2026 midterms. See the turnout by county 
 The county with the highest early voter turnout was Williamson, at about 38%. 
 By Chasity Maynard Published : Nov. 2, 2026 at 4:51 PM CST | Updated : 4 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google What This Story Is About 
 Tennessee saw a surge in early voter turnout this Midterm season. 
 Why It Matters 
 The Tennessee Secretary of State’s Office is reporting that turnout is over 45% ahead of what the state saw during the same time frame in 2022. 
 What Happens Next 
 Election Day is Tuesday . It’s the last chance for voters to cast ballots in the 2026 midterms. 
 For Context 
 The county with the highest early voter turnout was Williamson, at about 38%. 
 Catch Up 
 See WSMV4’s comprehensive coverage of the 2026 election results here . 
 Follow along as votes are tabulated here . 
 NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - Tennessee saw a surge in early voter turnout this Midterm season. 
 The Tennessee Secretary of State’s Office is reporting that turnout is over 45% ahead of what the state saw during the same time frame in 2022. 
 On day 14 of early voting four years ago, Tennessee reported 882,310 votes. But by day 14 of this year, which was Thursday, Tennessee reported nearly 1.3 million votes.
 Hover over or click on each county to see how this year’s turnout compares to year’s past. 
 That’s nearly 400,000 more people turning out to the polls. It also amounts to about 27% of all registered voters in Tennessee. 
 The county with the highest early voter turnout was Williamson. About 38% of voters there cast their ballots early. The county with the lowest early voter turnout was Hancock, at about 12%.
 See how your county ranked below. 
 In Davidson County, about 29.8% of voters showed up to the polls early this year, according to the Davidson County Election Commission . 
 The most ballots were cast at the Hermitage Library. 
 Hover over each icon to see more about that voting location.
